manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the phone on the box and place it on the phone stand to the right.

Task description: The target phone has a black screen and white frame and rests on the white box on the left. Its target is the white phone stand to the box's right, with a gray backrest and lower hooks. Transfer the phone onto it so it rests stably.

Success criteria: The phone is securely supported by the phone stand on the right and remains stably on the stand after the gripper opens, without slipping or tipping.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping the middle of both long edges of the phone, leaving the end that will go into the hook exposed. The opening only needs to be slightly wider than the phone; watch the nearby pen to avoid brushing it with the fingers.
- The phone lies close to the box surface. Before closing, confirm the fingers are on opposite sides and the pads cover the frame height, avoiding merely pressing the screen or gripping the box. If the phone slips during lifting, let the box surface support it again before adjusting the grasp.
- When adjusting the phone tilt, choose a location with clearance around it so all four corners and the gripper fingers stay away from the box, pen, and stand, avoiding contact while turning.
- Near the stand, tilt the phone's back along the backplate and lower its bottom edge into the support hooks, avoiding their outer edges. Leave clearance for finger withdrawal and release gently once the phone is securely supported, reducing the risk of moving the phone or stand during withdrawal.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this authorized real-robot episode with the given parameters, follow the manual and live observations, and call finish_episode when ending.

I have confirmed the target phone and stand on the right; only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the approach pose at a high position, then will use small movements to check grasp positions on both sides of the phone.

The phone is still on the box, with no contact yet. The live joint state indicates that I need to descend while adjusting pitch. I will keep clearance above the object and avoid the pen beside the phone.

The last step hit the controller's position limit, so the arm completed only part of the move. I replanned using the returned measured position and lowered the height. The phone has not been contacted; I will continue adjusting to a reachable pose within this episode.

The gripper is near the phone from above, with its long-edge direction roughly aligned. Next, each translation will be no greater than 1 cm. I will first correct lateral position and height, closing only after confirming pads at both frame edges.

Both fingers are on opposite sides of the phone's long edges, near the middle. I will close slightly first, then test-lift a short distance and use the view to confirm whether the phone moves with the gripper.

During the test lift, the phone did not clearly leave the box surface with the gripper, so the grasp is not reliable. I returned it to the supported position, and will open the gripper, lower the pads slightly, and check again.

During this test lift, the phone remained stable relative to the gripper, and the image shows it clear of the box surface. I will first increase clearance, then adjust its tilt and move it toward the stand on the right.
The phone remains grasped and has started moving toward the stand. I am maintaining sufficient clearance above the box and gradually turning the phone to an angle suitable for the backboard.

The phone remains securely grasped. The wrist rotation is approaching its joint limit, so I will first lift it on the left side of the stand, adjust to a reachable placement pose, then approach the hooks.

I have realigned the phone with the backrest at a higher position; gripper opening and relative phone position show no obvious change. Next I will gradually lower toward the hooks and check whether the lower edge enters the support position.

The descending pose needed for portrait placement remains near the wrist limit. I will rotate the phone to landscape at height and use both side hooks for support. Success still depends on whether it remains stable on the stand after release.

The phone is gradually turning at a raised height, with no visible slipping. In this horizontal pose, the lower gripper finger will pass between the two support hooks; I will check that clearance during approach before deciding whether to release.
The horizontal orientation is complete, and the phone remains held. I am descending in steps of 1 cm; the head camera shows a remaining gap between the phone and backboard.

The phone is near the backboard, and its position relative to the gripper changed slightly in the image. I will pause to recheck, then use smaller steps to confirm contact and hook positions; I will not release it yet.

The phone's lower edge is near hook height, but the head view shows that support on both sides is not fully aligned. I will first translate slightly along its long edge so both hooks lie within the lower-edge span, then continue lowering.

The current view shows the lower edge of the phone has reached the support hook and its back is near the backboard. I will loosen the gripper slightly to check the support, then confirm the phone remains stable after the fingers withdraw.

After slightly loosening the gripper, the phone settled a little and remained still; opening the gripper further did not cause it to slide. I will slowly withdraw the fingers and check whether the phone remains stable on the stand on its own.

The gripper is open and withdrawn. During the observation wait, the phone remained on the stand without further sliding or tipping. I will end this episode; final success requires on-site operator confirmation.
